cards.subject: St. John Bosco, priest, half-length, in a black Piedmontese cassock with a small white collar, one arm around the shoulder of a smiling boy of about twelve in a jacket, holding a rosary in his other hand; above them, small in the sky, an image of Mary Help of Christians. Background: Turin, the domed Basilica of Mary Help of Christians at Valdocco with the Alps beyond.
cards.face: A sturdy man of about fifty with a square, clean-shaven face, broad high cheekbones, thick wavy dark-brown hair with the first grey, brushed back from the forehead, lively dark eyes and a broad, warm, fatherly smile.
cards.basis: His photographs, above all the one taken in Turin in 1880: a square peasant face, prominent cheekbones, curly hair brushed back and a broad smile. We take him at about fifty and leave out the tiredness of the last photographs.

cards.face: A woman of about forty with a soft, round, fair face, grey-blue eyes, gently arched light-brown brows, rosy cheeks and a warm, quiet smile; her gaze is lifted a little upward.
cards.basis: No portrait or description survives; Gregory's Dialogues give only her love, her prayer and the dove. The face is an artistic choice that keeps her apart from the other nuns of this batch: younger, round-faced and smiling.

cards.subject: Pope St. Pius X, half-length, in the white papal cassock and white zucchetto with a red mozzetta, a red stole and a gold pectoral cross on a cord; he holds a small golden ciborium and raises a white Host toward a little girl of about seven in a white First Communion veil, who kneels at the lower edge with folded hands. Background: the Vatican gardens with the dome of St. Peter's in the distance.
cards.face: A man of about seventy with a broad, handsome, open face and strong clear-cut features, clean-shaven, thick short silver-white hair under the white zucchetto, clear light eyes under straight brows and a kind, winning smile.
cards.basis: His photographs as pope, and witnesses quoted by Forbes (1918): a 'handsome open face and strong clear-cut features', eyes full of light and a 'winning smile'. The Host and the child stand for his decree on early First Communion.

cards.subject: St. Teresa Benedicta of the Cross (Edith Stein), half-length, in the brown habit of a Discalced Carmelite with a black veil, white wimple and the white Carmelite mantle; she holds a plain wooden cross against her breast and a closed book in her other hand, with a martyr's palm beside her. Background: Cologne, with the twin spires of the cathedral above the rooftops and the Rhine.
cards.face: A mature woman of about forty-seven (NOT a young girl): a strong, broad, square-jawed face with high cheekbones, thick dark straight eyebrows, deep-set dark intelligent eyes, a straight nose and full, composed lips; a grave, thoughtful, scholarly expression with a faint gentle warmth. She must look clearly older and more serious than Thérèse and Teresa of Ávila.
cards.basis: Her photographs, above all the passport photograph taken at the door of the Cologne Carmel in 1938–39: dark heavy brows, deep-set dark eyes, a strong nose and a grave expression. She died at fifty.

cards.subject: Sts. Martha, Mary and Lazarus, three figures half-length side by side, all with haloes, all inside the arched window. Left, Martha in a russet-red gown with a white head-cloth and a bunch of keys at her girdle, holding a small earthenware jug. Centre, Lazarus, a little behind his sisters, in a plain off-white robe with a linen cloth over one shoulder, his hand on his heart. Right, Mary of Bethany with her long dark hair loose and uncovered (NO veil, NO blue mantle: she must not look like the Virgin Mary), in a rose-coloured gown with a green cloak, holding a small alabaster jar of ointment. Background: the village of Bethany on the slope of the Mount of Olives, a stone house with a vine at the door, Jerusalem faint in the distance.
cards.face: Martha: a woman of about thirty-five, strong and wholesome, with a round face, rosy cheeks, chestnut hair tucked under the head-cloth, steady brown eyes and a frank, kindly look toward the viewer. Mary: a younger woman of about twenty-five, with a delicate oval face, long dark wavy hair loose over her shoulders, large dark eyes lowered to the alabaster jar and a still, listening expression. Lazarus: a lean man of about fifty with a pale, gaunt, gentle face, receding short grey-streaked black hair, clean-shaven and dark eyes raised in quiet gratitude; not curly-haired, not long-haired.
cards.basis: No tradition fixes their faces, so the three are set apart by age, colouring and attribute, following the Gospel roles the 2021 decree names: Martha serving, Mary listening, Lazarus raised. Mary is kept veiled and dark-haired so she does not repeat the Magdalene card.

sources.title: Decree on the celebration of Saints Martha, Mary and Lazarus in the General Roman Calendar (26 January 2021)

Golden Legend (Caxton), Life of S. Martha

cards.subject: Sts. Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen, two Greek bishops half-length side by side, both with haloes, inside the arched window. Left, Basil in a dark green-gold phelonion with the white omophorion marked with black crosses, holding an unrolled scroll of the Divine Liturgy. Right, Gregory in a rose-red phelonion with the same white omophorion, holding a closed jewelled Gospel book against his chest. Background: Cappadocia, the rocky hills and fairy-chimney rocks near Caesarea, with snow-capped Mount Argaeus in the distance.
cards.face: Two clearly different people. Basil: a lean ascetic man in his late forties; a LONG, NARROW face with a high forehead, a long thin aquiline nose with a pronounced bridge, close-set deep-set dark eyes under high-arched black brows, hollow cheeks, thin lips; thick dark hair threaded with grey; a long black beard narrowing to a point. Gregory: a man of about sixty with a BROAD, ROUND, FLESHY face, a short wide nose with a rounded tip, large wide-set soft eyes with heavy lids, full cheeks and a full lower lip; bald crown with a short fringe at the sides; a broad square-cut smoky dark-grey beard; a gentle, meditative look.
cards.basis: The Painter's Manual gives Basil grey hair, a large beard and arched brows, and Gregory baldness and a broad beard 'of a sooty colour'; the Kiev mosaic of Basil and the Chora fresco of Gregory show the same types. Basil is kept dark-haired to separate the pair.

sources.title: Didron, Manuel d'iconographie chrétienne (1845), p. 316 (Dionysius of Fourna)

cards.subject: St. Anthony the Abbot, half-length, in a coarse grey-brown tunic under a black hooded mantle, the hood drawn up over his head, a blue tau cross on the shoulder of the mantle; he leans on a tall T-shaped (tau) staff hung with a small bell and holds an open book; a small pink pig at the lower edge. Background: the Egyptian desert by the Red Sea mountains, a cave mouth, a spring and a few date palms.
cards.face: A very old but hale hermit with a TRIANGULAR face: broad weathered brow, very prominent high cheekbones, sunken temples, a narrow pointed chin under the beard; small deep-set eyes narrowed as against the desert sun with deep crow's-feet; a short, broad, slightly flattened nose; a wide thin mouth. Deeply sun-browned skin. The black hood frames the face so no hair shows; a medium-length grey-white beard parted at the chin into two points; bushy white brows; a calm, bright gaze.
cards.basis: The Painter's Manual gives him as an old man with a short beard parted in two; the Greek icons, like Damaskinos's, show him hooded. Athanasius says he kept his sight and bodily health to the end; the tau, bell and pig are the Western card attributes.

sources.title: Didron, Manuel d'iconographie chrétienne (1845), p. 330 (Dionysius of Fourna)

cards.subject: St. Polycarp, bishop and martyr, half-length, bareheaded, in a white chasuble with a narrow red pallium, holding a Gospel book and a martyr's palm; behind him a tall arch of golden flames curves over him like a ship's sail filled with wind, leaving him untouched and serene. Background: Smyrna, its harbour and the hill of Mount Pagos, under a clear sky.
cards.face: A very old man of about eighty-five with a SMALL, HEART-SHAPED face: wide cheekbones tapering to a small pointed chin, round rosy apple cheeks, a small short upturned nose, small bright eyes crinkled by a gentle smile, a short upper lip; a full head of soft thin silvery-white hair falling to the nape (not bald); a short, neat, rounded snow-white beard; eyes raised to heaven with a quiet smile.
cards.basis: The Painter's Manual gives 'an old man, rounded beard', and the Martyrdom gives his age, eighty-six years in Christ's service, and the fire shaped 'like the sail of a ship'. The full white hair is an artistic choice to keep him apart from the bald elders on existing cards.

sources.title: Didron, Manuel d'iconographie chrétienne (1845), p. 318 (Dionysius of Fourna)

cards.subject: St. Hildegard of Bingen, abbess, half-length, in the black Benedictine habit with a black veil over a white wimple, an abbess's crozier resting against her shoulder; she holds a wax writing tablet and a stylus, and golden tongues of fire descend from an opening in the sky onto her head. Background: the Rhine at Bingen, with the abbey of Rupertsberg above the river and vine-covered hills.
cards.face: A woman of about sixty-five with a long, noble, narrow face, a strong straight nose, fine lines at the eyes, thin silver-grey brows, deep-set brown eyes raised upward toward the light, and firm, composed lips.
cards.basis: No portrait from life survives; the Rupertsberg Scivias shows her receiving the fiery light with a wax tablet while Volmar writes. She described that light filling her in 1141, at forty-two, and wrote her last visions in old age, so the face is an older abbess, kept apart from the other nuns of this batch.

cards.subject: St. Rita of Cascia, half-length, in the black Augustinian habit with a black veil, a white wimple and a leather belt; she gazes at a crucifix she holds in her hands, from which one fine golden ray reaches a small thorn-mark on her forehead; a single red rose lies beside the crucifix. Background: the Umbrian hills at Cascia with the town and the monastery of St. Mary Magdalene, and a vine.
cards.face: A woman of about fifty-five with a pale, fine-boned, slightly long face, a small dark thorn-mark in the middle of the forehead kept small and neat, dark-brown eyes lifted in sorrowful love to the crucifix, a slender straight nose and gentle, closed lips.
cards.basis: The portrait on the casket made for her body in 1457 shows a long, pale, older face with the forehead wound; the wound, the rose and the crucifix are her constant marks. The black habit follows the popular devotional image rather than the brown of her monastery.
